_note: Skeleton for docs/ledger-no-shrink-exemptions.json — the factory data file read by tests/test_ledger_no_shrink.py. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and add an entry ONLY when a row removal has an EMPTY REPAIR SPACE: the commit is pushed and cannot be amended (rewriting it is barred by the identity law), a revert cannot clear a gate that walks the committed lineage, and no lawful path restores the identity — the ledger is append-only, so a retired identity is restored by APPENDING a row naming it, never by deleting. Key every entry by the FULL 40-character sha copied from live git output — a short sha or a tag matches nothing while looking like it should. The entry must PROVE the empty repair space and state the reason, ideally naming the ruling that sanctions the removal. It is printed as an 'excused:' line on EVERY gate run, so it is a visible debt rather than forgiveness, and the closing line distinguishes clean from excused. A malformed entry, or one that matches no removal, is a gate ERROR rather than a silent pass. Expect this list to stay near-empty: the lawful path never deletes a row, so a deletion needs no annotation to be evidence and an exemption is the rare case where the removal is already on the record.
